items.title: Peel Police Investigate After Car Carrying Two People Hits Mississauga Bus Shelter
items.summary: According to Insauga, a vehicle crashed into a bus shelter in Mississauga on Friday morning, leaving the structure collapsed and glass scattered across the sidewalk. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told the outlet the vehicle, which was occupied by a driver and one passenger, struck the shelter on Oct. 9. Police said the investigation into the collision and the circumstances surrounding it remains ongoing. Photos from the scene show a silver vehicle resting on the sidewalk next to the destroyed shelter. Insauga reports this isn't the first time a bus shelter in Peel Region has been hit by a vehicle, pointing to a September 2024 multi-vehicle crash at Derry Road West and Terragar Boulevard in Meadowvale West that left one pedestrian with minor injuries. The outlet also noted a June crash this year in which a bus shelter was destroyed and a light pole damaged after one driver fled the scene.

items.title: Peel Police Called In After Man Tries to Jump Costco Pokemon Card Line in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police were called to a Mississauga Costco near Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street early Friday morning after a man tried to cut into a lineup forming ahead of a new Pokemon card release. Social media posts had circulated word that Costco Canada's Ascended Heroes Mini Tin 5-Packs were expected to drop at select stores on Oct. 9, including the Laird Road location in Mississauga and a Newmarket store. Insauga reports officers were brought in to help manage the crowd that gathered in anticipation of the release. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told the outlet officers were on a paid duty assignment monitoring the lineup when one person reportedly tried to take a spot ahead of others waiting. Insauga reports the incident reflects the lengths some collectors will go to secure sought-after Pokemon card products as demand for new releases continues to drive early-morning crowds at retailers.

items.title: Mississauga Man's Three Decades of Playing the Lottery Finally Pay Off With $500K Lump Sum
items.summary: According to Insauga, Dennis, a 50-year-old Mississauga man who has played the lottery for about 30 years, is weighing what to do with a windfall after winning big through the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation. OLG says Dennis matched all five main numbers in the Sept. 3 Daily Grand draw to win the second prize of $25,000 a year for life, and chose a lump-sum payment of $500,000 instead of the annuity. Dennis told OLG the experience felt truly out of this world and that the feeling was unreal. He said he picked up coffee, had breakfast at home and decided to check his tickets before realizing what had happened, recalling that he could not process it at first. While collecting his winnings at the OLG Prize Centre in Toronto, Dennis said he told his mother first, and that she thought he was joking until it sank in. Insauga reports Dennis plans to save and invest the money for the future rather than rush into any major decisions.

items.title: A Creemore Jail Visit Leads Modern Mississauga Writer to a 19th-Century Local Land Deal
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, a recent road trip to Collingwood turned into an unexpected history lesson when the writer stopped in Creemore and visited what's reportedly the smallest jail in North America, the Little Lock-up, built in 1894. Nearby stands Claverleigh, a National Historic Site built in 1871 as a rectory for Reverend William Rabbath Forster, who also directed construction of Creemore's St. Luke's Anglican Church in 1887. The outlet reports Forster purchased 100 acres in Lot 32, Concession 2, north of Dundas Street, on May 24, 1850, shortly after arriving in Canada, and sold the property to his brother Frederick Forster in 1855. That same parcel of land in historic Mississauga is where Millennium Grove and Dunn Park now sit along Erin Mills Parkway, north of Burnhamthorpe Road. Modern Mississauga Media says the find was one of several unexpected connections back to Mississauga turned up during the writer's meandering road trip north.

items.title: Four Candidates, Including a Longtime Incumbent, Compete for Peel School Board Seats in Mississauga Wards 6 and 11
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, incumbent trustee Jill Promoli faces three challengers, Patrick Khrenaron Ma, Harish Shroff and Shashi Singh, for the Peel District School Board seats representing Mississauga wards 6 and 11 in the Oct. 26 election. The outlet said it sent a questionnaire to every candidate on the ballot to help voters get to know them ahead of the vote. Candidate Patrick Khrenaron Ma, who works in accounting, personal tax and small business, told Mississauga.com he has lived in the city for 22 years and considers it the only place he'd want to be. Ma said his priority as trustee would be advocating for students and their families while making sure PDSB schools remain safe and inclusive places to learn. Mississauga.com reports the race gives Wards 6 and 11 voters a choice between continuity with the sitting trustee and three newcomers seeking a seat on the school board.

items.title: Open Ward 7 Council Seat Draws Field of 17 After Incumbent Enters Mayoral Race
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, 17 candidates are competing for Ward 7's open council seat after sitting councillor Dipika Damerla left to run for mayor in the Oct. 26 municipal election. The outlet said candidates who didn't respond to its questionnaire had their information pulled from the City of Mississauga's certified candidates list instead. One candidate highlighted a decade working in crime prevention and the non-profit sector, including time managing neighbourhood safety programs, and said growing up in Mississauga shaped a lasting connection to the city. That candidate said priorities include improving community safety through data-informed engagement strategies that bring Peel police, non-profits and the city together, along with building up resident associations to give tenants and condo residents a stronger voice. Mississauga.com reports the crowded Ward 7 race reflects a broader reshuffling of council as Damerla's mayoral run opened up one of the city's most contested seats.

items.title: Ontario Election Officials Hope 2026 Reverses a Slide in Municipal Voter Turnout
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, only about one third of eligible voters cast ballots in Ontario's 2022 municipal elections, continuing a decline that officials are hoping to reverse when voters head to the polls again on Oct. 26. The outlet reports the Association of Municipalities of Ontario, a collective representing the province's towns and cities, believes the low 2022 turnout was partly tied to the COVID-19 pandemic and is hoping participation recovers this time around. AMO data spanning three decades shows provincewide turnout has typically stayed above 40 per cent, with the last two election cycles standing out as the only ones to fall below that mark. Mississauga.com notes municipal elections were held every three years until 2006, when the province shifted to the current four-year cycle. The outlet reports turnout reached as high as 48 per cent back in 1982, underscoring how far participation has fallen since then.

items.title: Mississauga Creates Temporary Task Force to Review Data Centre Rules While Building Pause Continues
items.summary: According to Ontario Construction News, Mississauga council has approved a motion to set up a temporary Hyperscale Data Centre Task Force as the city reviews its policies and regulations covering major digital infrastructure facilities. The outlet reports the task force follows council's Sept. 16 approval of an interim control bylaw that paused processing of new and existing applications for major digital infrastructure facilities for up to a year. That pause is giving city staff time to carry out a comprehensive review of planning policies, zoning rules and development approval processes tied to data centres. The new task force will give council members, city planning staff, industry stakeholders and citizen members a forum for regular updates and input during that review. Ontario Construction News reports the group is also meant to support public transparency and reporting as the process moves forward. Any recommendations that come out of the review will go back to council for consideration, and the task force will be dissolved once that review wraps up and council has weighed in.

items.title: Crombie Wants to Halt Study of Demolishing Mississauga's Living Arts Centre
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, Mississauga mayoral candidates staked out competing positions on the future of the Living Arts Centre on Thursday as the municipal election entered its final two and a half weeks. Incumbent Bonnie Crombie said she wants to stop further study into potentially demolishing the downtown venue as part of a large redevelopment project, calling it a vanity project the city cannot justify while residents struggle with everyday bills. She told reporters any municipal funding set aside for that study should instead be redirected to other city priorities. The Living Arts Centre sits just north of Mississauga city hall and west of Square One, and has operated since opening in 1997. The venue includes a 1,300-seat main auditorium along with several meeting rooms and exhibition spaces used for community and cultural events. CityNews reports the dispute over the centre's future emerged as candidates continued rolling out policy platforms ahead of the Oct. 26 election.

items.title: SIU Clears Peel Police in Death of Man Who Fell From Mississauga Balcony This Summer
items.summary: According to the Special Investigations Unit, the provincial watchdog has closed its investigation into the death of a man who fell from the balcony of a Mississauga condo this past summer, finding police had no chance to save him. The SIU said Peel officers were dispatched to a building on Kingsbridge Garden Circle, near Highway 403, after a woman called police on July 29 to report her boyfriend had assaulted her. The SIU said officers knocked on the unit's door, identified themselves and called out the man's name, but got no answer. According to the SIU's account, the 34-year-old man placed a chair near the balcony railing and was seen climbing onto it. The agency said an officer moved toward the sliding glass door and called out for the man to stop, but he fell before officers could reach him. The SIU is automatically called in whenever a death or serious injury occurs during an interaction between police and the public, and its investigation concluded officers were not at fault in this case.

items.title: Ward 7 Candidate Jerry Krzywda Says Affordability and Safe Streets Drove Him to Run
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, Ward 7 council candidate Jerry Krzywda says he's running because his family has deep roots in the ward, where he's now raising his own children after his family immigrated from Poland when he was six. Krzywda told the outlet he spent part of his childhood in Cooksville and considers Ward 7 home. He said he wants the ward to be a place where residents, whether renting or owning, can afford to live and build a future, where seniors can stay in the communities they know, and where people can count on safe streets, well-maintained public spaces and dependable city services. The profile is part of Modern Mississauga Media's 2026 election series, which invited every candidate to answer the same set of questions ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal vote. The outlet said the series aims to boost voter turnout after historically low engagement, noting candidates were asked to submit at least four images alongside their unedited answers. Modern Mississauga Media said it will continue posting candidate profiles as they come in, with each one published within 72 hours of being received.

items.title: Mississauga Reconstructing Two North-End Trails to Add Up to 25 Years of Life
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the city is reconstructing two popular trails in its north end as part of an effort to extend their service life by up to 25 years. The city said in a project update that the improvements aim to create safer, more accessible connections throughout the surrounding neighbourhood, supporting walking, cycling, recreation and everyday travel. Ward 9 Coun. Martin Reid said residents should expect the ongoing construction to cause temporary trail closures while the work is underway. The city said the reconstructed trails will be built to current municipal standards, providing reliable, low-maintenance infrastructure for the community. Officials said the upgrades are expected to extend the trails' service life by roughly 20 to 25 years while reducing future maintenance needs. The city said it will post advance notice signs to alert residents to any upcoming temporary closures or construction activity that could affect them.
